desc: Livermore is the second nuclear design laboratory, founded in 1952 at Edward Teller's urging as a competitor to Los Alamos, and administered since 1 October 2007 by Lawrence Livermore National Security, LLC - a consortium including the University of California and Bechtel. It was funded at approximately 2,188.8 million dollars in FY2024. Its place on this board is structural rather than evidentiary. Livermore holds the national capability in high-energy-density physics, advanced materials characterisation, and directed energy - precisely the disciplines any exploitation programme would need - and it operates under Q clearance and DOE's separate Restricted Data classification regime, which is the one authority in the US system that is not derived from executive order and therefore not reachable by a presidential declassification directive alone. That distinction matters enormously in 2026: the PURSUE releases proceed under executive authority, but material classified as Restricted Data under the Atomic Energy Act does not move on that authority. No document has been produced placing Livermore in any UAP programme. It is catalogued here because the Atomic Energy Act pathway is the most plausible remaining legal shelter for a concealed programme after the executive-order pathway has been opened, and Livermore is one of the three laboratories that live inside it.
